reviewer: Codex author of cet-reading-001; same author, not an independent teacher or learner panel
approvalScope: Author passage-entailment, unique-key and all-distractor review of eight unpublished candidate practices. Does not assert publication, production deployment, independent review, official CET provenance or psychometric calibration.
audienceModel: CET4/CET6 learners need readable, concrete original cases and a uniquely passage-supported best answer. Chinese explanations identify why each competing option is unsupported, contradicted, too broad or a different claim.
authoringMethod: Eight distinct passages and all eighty prompts, four-option sets, keys and Chinese explanations were explicitly authored. Code serializes authored content, checks format and reorders answer positions; it does not invent or template passages/questions.
caseBoundary: The institute, care service, planning district, museum collaboration and other named local cases are invented educational scenarios. Passage-supported interpretation is tested; no external factual knowledge or inaccessible media is required.
wordCountMethod: English alphabetic words; internal apostrophes or hyphens form one word; titles excluded. Regex: \b[A-Za-z]+(?:['’-][A-Za-z]+)*\b

findings: Q1 and Q2 distinguish selective circulation from absent recordkeeping, and a bounded test record from a sustained journal argument.

units.approvalScope: Same-author semantic/content review of this candidate only; not release approval.
findings: Q1 and Q2 require a stated no-project baseline; energy savings from independently planned pump closure cannot all be attributed to restoration.
Q3 does not assign new crop removal to fields already idle. Q4’s displaced production is conditional, not a claim that every marsh project necessarily shifts emissions.
Q5 scenarios expose alternative assumptions and are not measurements to average. Q6 and Q7 preserve immediate construction costs and long-term expected accumulation.
Q8 requires temporal and causal boundaries. Q9 recognises habitat benefits separately rather than converting them into carbon. Q10 distinguishes conditional approval from verified future outcomes.
